basis.selection: Inspect k=7 because it is the second-highest mean-silhouette candidate and separates recognizable cancellation, fulfillment, product, and reporting groups. Seed 0 has the highest silhouette within k=7. This is an explicit human selection for architectural inspection.

rationale: The highest average silhouette selects k=2; its best run places 41 clauses together and isolates two product-search clauses. A seven-cluster candidate exposes more useful responsibilities and several mixed groups. The reviewed proposal assigns six application-core components and one channel boundary using source obligations, state ownership, and the three scenario walkthroughs. Its boundaries are human decisions, not a claim that the embedding model discovered this exact architecture.

components.name: Product Catalog
components.responsibility: Describe products, recursive breakfast packages, unit prices, and public product discovery.
components.owns: Product definitions, package composition, units, prices, unique product codes, and search criteria.

components.name: Customer Eligibility
components.responsibility: Identify customers, verify their identity and eligibility, and supply the predefined delivery address.
components.owns: Customer identity, customer-number format, credentials, blacklist status, and the single predefined address.

components.name: Order Lifecycle
components.responsibility: Create orders and blueprints and enforce the authoritative order state and cancellation rules.
components.owns: Cart/order lines, one-customer ownership, blueprint links, order numbers, immutable submitted order snapshots, and lifecycle state.

components.name: Packing and Delivery
components.responsibility: Support packing, courier assignment, bag labels, multi-order itineraries, and authenticated delivery confirmation.
components.owns: Packing work allocation, assigned delivery clerk, bag-label rendering, itinerary plans, and delivery-confirmation evidence. Order Lifecycle remains authoritative for lifecycle transitions.

components.name: Documents and Payment Exchange
components.responsibility: Produce separately numbered invoice copies and transfer expected-payment records on committed assembly completion.
components.owns: Invoice-copy identity and rendering, expected-payment interface records, and transfer tracking. The existing payment processor remains external.

components.name: Daily Business Reporting
components.responsibility: Assemble and print the manager's complete daily business report on the nightly schedule.
components.owns: Reporting projection, report-day selection, schedule configuration, and report rendering/printing. Business-day policy remains unresolved.

components.name: Web and SMS Entry Points
components.responsibility: Translate web and SMS requests and responses into shared core operations.
components.owns: Web forms, SMS C/W/P and O syntax, SMS transport limits, gateway integration, and channel response formatting.

decisions.title: D01 · Choose an interpretable candidate rather than treating silhouette as a verdict
decisions.reason: The k=2 reference isolates the two product-search clauses while placing the other 41 together. Its mean silhouette is 0.0698 and seed agreement is 0.1355. k=7 has mean silhouette 0.0620 and agreement 0.2686. The latter is more informative to inspect, but the low agreement prevents presenting its exact partition as established truth.

decisions.title: D02 · Split the identifiers/channel cluster by owned knowledge
decisions.reason: Candidate cluster 4 mixes customer numbers/addresses, order numbers, product codes, channels, and payment-record fields. Assign these to Customer Eligibility, Order Lifecycle, Product Catalog, channel entry points, and Payment Exchange according to the business knowledge each owns. Shared identifier vocabulary is not a shared responsibility.

decisions.title: D03 · Keep one authoritative lifecycle across cancellation and assembly
decisions.reason: Candidate cluster 0 contains cancellation rules while cluster 1 contains assembly/payment activity. Keep the order's authoritative state in Order Lifecycle. Packing reports completion through a guarded transition; Billing consumes the committed assembly trigger. The atomicity and reliable-transfer mechanism are engineering decisions derived from the source.

decisions.title: D04 · Separate print-copy behavior from the payment trigger
decisions.reason: The candidate spreads invoices across clusters 1 and 5 and payment across 1 and 4. Group the financial document and exchange responsibilities with distinct operations: every print gets a new copy number, while only assembly completion triggers an expected-payment transfer. Co-location does not imply shared triggering.

decisions.title: D05 · Keep blueprint rules with orders; return unrelated constraints to their owners
decisions.reason: Candidate cluster 5 mixes blueprint reuse with unit pricing, invoice-copy numbers, and SMS limits. Keep blueprint links and their cardinalities in Order Lifecycle, unit pricing in Product Catalog, print-copy identity in Billing, and SMS limits at the channel edge.

decisions.title: D06 · Distinguish public search from authenticated ordering and handover
decisions.reason: Candidate cluster 6 groups access-related wording but includes three different workflows. Customer Eligibility verifies identity and blacklist status; Order Lifecycle assembles carts; Fulfillment owns delivery confirmation; Product Catalog permits public search. The shared word 'customer' does not force one component.

decisions.title: D07 · Keep reporting together and make its reads explicit
decisions.reason: Candidate cluster 3 already isolates nightly report scheduling and content. Preserve that responsibility. A reporting projection avoids making source modules depend on report layout, but projection freshness and the business-day cutoff require explicit policies.

decisions.title: D08 · Separate product definitions from customer selection and order lines
decisions.reason: Candidate cluster 2 groups breakfast composition and discovery. Product Catalog owns package definitions and filtering. Order Lifecycle owns the customer's chosen items and quantities, preserving the distinction between a reusable product definition and an order instance.
